Modern.brandNameRationale: Ledger is the oldest word in finance. It predates banks. It predates currency. We named the brand after the original act of writing down what is owed and what is held. One word. Direct. Trusted by association.
Modern.industrySummary: Consumer fintech has stopped being novelty and started being infrastructure. People expect a clean app, fast transfers, and clear fees. The bar for design and clarity is high. The winners are the brands that read the simplest.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Wise (wise.com) carries the international clarity. Mercury (mercury.com) owns the business banking design language. Monzo (monzo.com) and Revolut (revolut.com) hold the consumer European space. Stripe (stripe.com) is the documentation gold standard. We sit between Mercury and Wise.
Modern.positioningStatement: Personal banking that explains every transaction the first time.
Modern.positioningRationale: Most banks hide things in legalese. We make the receipt the brand. Every transaction, every fee, every transfer is written in plain English. The brand promise lives inside the app, not on the homepage.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Has at least two accounts, one of which is for freelance income. Reads the fine print. Asks customer support pointed questions. Tells friends about the app if it works.

dos: Write transaction descriptions in plain English
Show the fee before it's charged
Speak to one customer at a time

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Ascot carries old-money association without saying so directly. The British racing town, the formal tie, the village that has been there a long time. Wealth closes it as a category. The pair reads as a private bank that already exists in a Mayfair townhouse.
Luxury.story: Ascot was founded by three partners who had spent twenty years inside large institutions and grew tired of the size. They wanted to manage fewer relationships, more carefully. The firm has never accepted more than fifty client families.
Luxury.industrySummary: Private wealth management at the top end is consolidating into larger groups. There's a parallel market for small, independent firms with fewer clients, more attention, and an older posture. We belong in that market.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Brown Brothers Harriman (bbh.com) is the institutional peer. Pictet (group.pictet) holds the Swiss reference. Stonehage Fleming (stonehagefleming.com) is the closest British peer. We are smaller than all of them, by intention.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A private wealth firm for fifty families. No more.

targetAudience.primary: Heads of family offices, founders post-exit, and inheritors who have outgrown their previous adviser. Looking for slow capital, considered counsel, and a relationship that lasts decades.

dos: Speak rarely
Address the principal by surname in writing
Send paper quarterly reports

Luxury.story: Eastbury Trust was founded in the late nineteenth century by two partners with a small private bank in the City. The firm has stayed small. Most clients are inherited. Most decisions are made by a single partner.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end private banking has been consolidating into larger institutions. There's a parallel market for small partner-led firms with multi-generational client relationships. Few clients, deep counsel, decades-long relationships.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: C. Hoare & Co. (hoaresbank.co.uk) holds the institutional heritage peer. Coutts (coutts.com) sits at the established peer. Brown Brothers Harriman (bbh.com) is the international peer. We sit smaller and quieter than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small private bank representing fewer than two hundred families.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Balance is what the customer is actually checking, and what most banking apps actively undermine with notifications and upsells. The brand is named after the thing they want to see.
Minimal.industrySummary: Fintech apps have been over-designed for years. Bright colors, animations, gamified savings goals. There's an opening for a brand that subtracts. One account. One screen. One thing it does well.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most consumer fintech competes on features. We compete on absence. The closest aesthetic peer is Charm Industrial's design language, but in a different category. There isn't a direct competitor in this position.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A bank account that does what a bank account does. Nothing else.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who already have a primary bank and want a secondary one with no marketing in their inbox. They want to send money, hold money, and check the balance. That's all.

dos: Use the smallest number of words
Show the balance and the recent transactions
Make the support email easy to find

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. BALANCE set in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps. No icon. The app icon is the wordmark abbreviated to BAL. No second mark.

typography.rationale: One face. One purpose. The app is the wordmark, the balance, the transactions. Nothing decorative.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No goals. No round-ups. No virtual cards. No referral program. No newsletter. No social media presence.

Minimal.brandDescription: A bank account that does what a bank account does. Nothing else.
Minimal.mission: To build a bank account that does what a bank account does. Nothing else.

Creative.brandNameRationale: A bank shot is a pool term and a basketball term. It's the skilled play that uses an angle to land the ball. The pun lands twice. Once at the door (the word bank), once at the back of the head (the play).
Creative.manifesto: Most fintech brands are quiet, clean, and slightly boring. We respect that. But there's a customer who wants their money app to have a personality. Someone who treats their finances seriously but talks about them with humor. We made Bank Shot for them.
Creative.industrySummary: Consumer fintech is dominated by sleek, monochrome, slightly cold apps. There's room for one that's warm, witty, and still serious about helping people handle their money. The category has been cold for too long.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Cash App (cash.app) figured out cultural relevance. Step (step.com) is the closest in playful tone. Cleo (cleo-ai.com) leans hard into personality. Albert (albert.com) had the tone for a moment. We're sharper and older in tone than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A finance app for people who want their money to be more fun to look at than to spend.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 40. Self-employed or salaried with side income. Already has a primary bank but wants a secondary tool that's actually nice to use. Follows two financial accounts on social and laughs at both of them.

dos: Make jokes about money without minimizing it
Talk like a friend who's good with finances
Use real numbers in copy, not stock figures

typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and UI
typography.rationale: Migra has personality. Neue Montreal handles the readable bits. The pair feels designed and a little weird.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a wealth manager. Not a crypto wallet. Not a get-rich-quick app. Not too cool to make a joke about itself.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: An app that's nice to open. Push notifications that feel like a friend texting. Stickers in welcome boxes. A monthly newsletter written like a group chat. Merch that people would actually wear.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Single word. Payday is the universal cultural moment in personal finance. The brand names the day everyone in the audience is waiting for. Loud, warm, immediately legible.
Creative.manifesto: Most fintech brands sell wealth, growth, transformation. We made Payday because the actual rhythm of most people's financial lives is the day the money comes in. The brand is for the moment of relief, the brief plan, the trip to the store, the bills paid. We are the brand for what payday actually is.
Creative.industrySummary: Fintech branding has been polished, growth-led, and slightly cold. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, and serious about the actual emotional rhythm of getting paid and spending.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Cash App (cash.app) figured out cultural relevance. Cleo (meetcleo.com) holds the friend-with-finances peer. Step (step.com) sits in the playful tone middle. Albert (albert.com) had the tone briefly. We sit warmer and more honest than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A finance app for people whose lives run on payday.

targetAudience.primary: 22 to 40. Lives between paychecks. Has a side income that pays sometimes. Wants the app to make payday feel as good as it actually is.
